title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no accessions, no GEO/SRA links; the only Zenodo hit on the DOI search is an unrelated repo (EEG-ECG music review agent). Listed the Paper2Agent GitHub repo root: only code, scripts, skills, assets, logo, README and LICENSE (MIT, 1,070 bytes); no data files.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the method (multi-agent construction of MCP (model context protocol) tool servers from papers, case studies on AlphaGenome, Scanpy, TISSUE and psoriasis gene prioritisation) comes from the abstract only; full text was not available.

a1_downloadable.note: Code is public on GitHub (MIT licence, checked). There is no dataset to download; the case studies reuse other papers' data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Killer. This is a software framework that wraps papers into AI agents; it releases no table of measurements and no prediction target. Any label (e.g. 'agent reproduced the result: yes/no') would have to be constructed by us from a handful of case studies.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table exists; inputs would be whole papers and codebases.

a5_enough_rows.note: Abstract describes a few case-study agents (AlphaGenome, Scanpy, TISSUE, psoriasis); far below any trainable count. No row count seen.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Nothing to load; the framework itself calls a hosted chat agent.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any evaluation label would be a judgement of an LLM (large language model) agent's output, not a physical measurement.

honest_claim_h3: None possible: the paper is a software tool and provides no labelled biological data to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a description of a research paper and its code to predict whether an automatically built AI assistant reproduces the paper's results.
plain_idea.train_on: Papers plus their code repositories; the number of examples with a reproduction outcome is unknown and, from the abstract, a handful of case studies.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the generated agent reproduces published results, which would come from the authors' or our own manual checks, not from a lab measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Tool builders would learn which papers are easy to turn into agents, but without a large labelled set this is not a biology ML project.

ml_idea: None viable. The only conceivable task (predicting agent reproduction success from paper/code features) has no released labels and a tiny number of examples.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the GitHub repo for any data/benchmark folder with per-paper outcomes (done: none exists).

verdict_reason: A software framework paper (Paper2Agent) that turns papers into AI agents; it releases code only (checked the GitHub repo) and no measured biological data or label column, so A2 fails.
